itinerary.cal: Climbed mostly from late spring into summer while the Squak Glacier is well covered; crevasses open up above about 8,700 ft as the season goes on. A free self-issued wilderness permit covers the Mount Baker Wilderness, and most parties take two days with a camp near Crag View, though it can be done in one long day.

days.note: Follow the Scott Paul trail to treeline and leave it for the moraine and ridge leading to the Crag View prow (about 6,500 ft); The Outbound puts this leg at about 2-4 hours. Parties camp just above or below the prow or at the glacier edge up to about 6,800 ft.
days.title: Schriebers Meadow to Crag View camp
days.objective: Reach camp at the edge of the Squak Glacier

days.note: Climb the Squak Glacier north, mostly crevasse-free to about 8,700 ft, then weave through a more crevassed and icier section to the saddle below the Roman Wall. Sherman's final slope can be very icy; descend the same way, pack up camp and walk out.
days.title: Climb the Squak Glacier to Sherman Peak

days.objective: Summit Sherman Peak and descend to the trailhead

itinerary.cal: July through September, once the Barrier crest and the Chopping Block ridge are mostly snow-free. A North Cascades National Park wilderness permit is required for the cross-country camps. Most parties take three days, or fold the peak into a longer Southern Pickets trip.

days.note: Follow the old roadbed up Goodell Creek, cross Terror Creek on a log near 2,000 ft, then take the climbers' path up the Barrier crest above timberline to the camp overlooking Crescent Creek Basin. One party leaving at 3 am reached camp well before noon. The alternative is to camp in Terror Basin (about 7 h from the car) and cross the Barrier on day 2 by a loose Class 3 grassy ledge.
days.title: Goodell Creek to Chopping Block ridge camp
days.objective: Carry to the ridge camp near 6,400 ft

days.note: Scramble Class 3 partway up the NE Ridge, make the exposed Class 4 ledge traverse across the north face (the route-finding is tricky), then go up easy Class 3 on the NW Ridge to the summit. Descend the NE Ridge with a few single-rope rappels.
days.title: Climb the Northwest Route
days.objective: Summit the Chopping Block and return to camp

days.note: Go down snow, slabs and heather to the Barrier crest at about 5,600 ft. A faint path follows the crest to about 3,600 ft, then the descent to the Terror Creek log is steep, brushy and cliffy. Back on the Goodell Creek path at 1,700 ft, follow it out to the trailhead at 600 ft. This took about 7 hours.
days.title: Descend the Barrier to Goodell Creek
days.objective: Return to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: Three days: a steep, brushy carry from Goodell Creek up the Barrier to the Chopping Block ridge camp, a short Class 4 summit day, then the long descent out.

itinerary.cal: Jul-Sep. Fit parties can climb Chianti car-to-car in a long day, as parties routinely do on the neighbouring Rebel Yell. A second Wine Spires objective, such as Burgundy Spire's North Face (5.8) or Paisano Pinnacle's West Ridge (5.8+), fits from the same camp. Little is known about this line, which argues for taking two days.

days.note: From the SR 20 pullout, drop about 300 ft to cross Early Winters Creek, then climb the climbers' trail to the 6,400-6,600 ft bench (standard low camp, with a spring) or on up loose gullies and a snow finger to Burgundy Col. The col is roughly 3.5 miles and 3,700 ft of gain away, 3-4 hours. Optionally climb a second Wine Spires objective.
days.title: Hike to Burgundy Col
days.objective: Camp on the bench or at Burgundy Col

days.note: From the col, descend 200-300 ft and traverse beneath Burgundy Spire's east face to Chianti's east face, under an hour. Lichen Bouquet's ramp starts directly below the summit and leans left. Descend toward the Burgundy-Chianti notch or rappel Rebel Yell with two 60 m ropes, regain the col, and hike out.
days.title: Climb Lichen Bouquet and hike out
days.objective: Climb the route, regain the col and hike out

itinerary.totalNote: Hike from SR 20 to the bench or Burgundy Col on day one, then traverse to Chianti's east face, climb Lichen Bouquet, and hike out on day two.

timing.recommendedStart: Camp at Upper Eagle Lake and leave camp at first light. The East Face takes morning sun and goes into shade by mid-afternoon, so an early start is both warmer on the rock and buys you the daylight you need for the walk-off scramble and the 6-mile hike out. If attempting it car-to-car, leave the Crater Creek trailhead pre-dawn.

itinerary.cal: Best done as an overnight from Upper Eagle Lake, which is what the first-ascent party did. A car-to-car day is possible for a strong, fast party but leaves no margin: it is about 13 trail-and-scramble miles with roughly 3,900 ft of gain plus four pitches of 5.10. You can also spend a second night at the lake and walk out fresh.

days.note: Hike the 6.2 miles of Eagle Lakes Trail #431 to Upper Eagle Lake (roughly 2 h 45 min of walking at the mapped trail estimate) and make camp among the established sites. Spend the last of the light scoping the East Face from the lakeshore; the crack systems are much easier to sort out with binoculars from the water than from the base.
days.title: Hike to Upper Eagle Lake
days.objective: Camp at the lake and scope the East Face

days.note: Leave camp at first light, scramble the 900-1,000 ft of talus and heather to the base, and climb the four pitches; budget generously, as the first-ascent party's climbing was very slow because of the cleaning required. Walk north to the summit, descend the standard scramble back to camp, then strike the tent and hike out.
days.title: Climb Tribute to Richard and hike out
days.objective: Climb the four pitches, summit, and return to the car

itinerary.totalNote: Hike 6.2 miles to Upper Eagle Lake and scope the East Face, then climb the four-pitch route, descend the standard scramble, and hike out on day two.

itinerary.cal: July through September. This is inside North Cascades National Park, so a backcountry permit is needed for a Blum Lakes camp. Parties usually plan three days and often add Mount Blum.

days.note: Leave the Baker River trail at Blum Creek and follow the faint, flagged climbers' path. It is brushy, then steep forest to about 4,500 ft, then a talus traverse near 4,900 ft to Lower Blum Lake and on to Upper Blum Lake. Stay on the path: the brush off it is very hard going. A winter party camped higher, at about 5,600 ft above the lakes.
days.title: Blum Creek path to Upper Blum Lake
days.objective: Climb from the Baker River trail to the lakes

days.note: Traverse from the lakes onto the Hagan Glacier side and work up to the high ground. One party dropped packs at a high pass and scrambled the last few hundred feet; a winter party reached the highest point by a bowl and a short, roughly 50-degree chute to the ridge. Published summit heights range from 6,960 to about 7,100 ft.
days.title: Hagan Glacier side to the summit
days.objective: Climb Hagan and return to camp

days.note: Reverse the steep climbers' path down Blum Creek. One party took about 2.5 hours down the path from the lakes; another lost the path below about 4,000 ft and found it again near Blum Creek.
days.title: Descend to the Baker River trail
days.objective: Hike out from Blum Lakes

itinerary.totalNote: Three days: a steep, brushy climbers' path to Upper Blum Lake, a day crossing the Hagan Glacier side to the summit, and the long descent back to the Baker River trail.

itinerary.cal: Climbed June through September; the Squire Creek ford and a tributary crossing are hard in early season or after storms. No permit is needed, and most parties take two days with a bivy at the grassy saddle at the start of the route.

days.note: Walk the old road past the Trail #654 sign to two cut logs with old cable, take the boot track down and ford Squire Creek, then follow the climbers' track downstream and up through old growth and two gullies. The top of the second gully is steep and dirty and opens onto the grassy saddle, which has good bivy sites near the route.
days.title: Squire Creek to the grassy saddle
days.objective: Reach the bivy at the base of the route

days.note: From the saddle, scramble down ramps for 20-30 m and cross the granite apron to a two-bolt anchor. The route has sustained 5.8 friction on pitches 2 and 7-10, and the last four pitches follow the Primal Scream ridge to a summit chain. Rappel the route on chain anchors; some rappels need a full 60 m rope. Carry a single rack to 3 inches.
days.title: Climb Concerto and rappel, hike out
days.objective: Climb 14 pitches to the summit crest and descend to the car

itinerary.totalNote: Two days: about 2-3 hours to the grassy-saddle bivy, then 14 pitches (1,800 ft) of mostly bolted slab and ridge, rappels back down the route, and the hike out.

timing.recommendedStart: Leave the road at first light on the approach day so you reach the glacier-toe bivouac with time to look at the face; start up the glacier at first light on the climbing day so the couloir is done and the south-side descent begun before afternoon sun softens everything.

itinerary.cal: Feb-Apr. Two days with one bivouac. Camping is not allowed at the Diablo townsite, so sleep the night before at a permitted backcountry site or in the Newhalem campground, and leave a car at the Gorge Creek bridge because the descent goes down the far side.

days.note: Leave at first light, hike the Stetattle Creek trail about 2 miles, and drop 200 ft to ford the creek opposite Davis. Bushwhack and scramble the 3rd/4th-class rib, roping up for the slabby sections, through slide alder to a bivouac on flat snow at the toe of the glacier at 4,000 ft, which has running water. Expect to arrive by late afternoon, roughly eight or nine hours from the road, and spend the evening judging whether the couloir will go.
days.title: Stetattle Creek to the glacier toe bivy
days.objective: Bivouac at the toe of the glacier

days.note: Go up the glacier at first light, gear up at the bergschrund, and climb the lower band, the snowfield, the crux pitches and the upper couloir to the summit ridge near 6,700 ft; tag the summit if there is time. Rappel from the top of the couloir onto the southeast ridge and commit to the full 6,000 ft south-side descent, aiming to be below the cliff bands before dark. Walk or shuttle the four road miles back to Diablo.

itinerary.totalNote: Day one bushwhacks from Diablo up the Stetattle Creek side to a bivy at the toe of the glacier; day two climbs the north face couloir and descends 6,000 ft down the south side to the Gorge Creek bridge.

itinerary.cal: A winter and spring ski-mountaineering line (Dec-Apr) that parties usually do in two days. A night at or above Cache Col needs an NPS wilderness permit from the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center; south of the col a free self-issue wilderness permit is enough.

days.note: Climb about 3.5 miles and 1,800 ft to Cascade Pass, then head south up the arm onto the gentle Cache Glacier. The December 2011 party reached a hollow about 500 ft below Cache Col at dark; a 2013 party pushed on to camp on Art's Knoll itself, and Kool-Aid Lake beyond the col is the summer option.

days.objective: Reach a camp on the Cache Glacier shoulder

days.note: Cross Cache Col in the dark to reach the saddle by Art's Knoll at first light, then drop to the Middle Cascade Glacier and climb the leftmost, slightly traversing snow line over the bergschrund. The last 100 m below the summit ridge is steep and can be icy enough to turn parties back. Retrace over Cache Col, break camp, and ski out over Cascade Pass.
